Because the line on which the upper CD lies is the tangent line of the left circle, and is tangent at the top of the left circle, the line on which CD lies is y=1. Let the center of the right circle be P=(1+t,1), then its diameter endpoints are C=(t,1), D=(t+2,1). The two circles with radius 1 are externally tangent, so the center distance OP=2. Thus the horizontal difference of OP is t, and the vertical difference is 1, so t^2+1^2=2^2, obtaining t^2=3. From the figure it can be seen that the right circle is on the right side, so t=√3. Because the line on which the upper CD lies is the tangent line of the left circle, and is tangent at the top of the left circle, the line on which CD lies is y=1. Let the center of the right circle be P=(1+t,1), then its diameter endpoints are C=(t,1), D=(t+2,1). The two circles with radius 1 are externally tangent, so the center distance OP=2. Thus the horizontal difference of OP is t, and the vertical difference is 1, so t^2+1^2=2^2, obtaining t^2=3. From the figure it can be seen that the right circle is on the right side, so t=√3. Thus D=(2+√3,1). Therefore AD^2=(2+√3)^2+1^2=4+4√3+3+1=8+4√3.
